summary: Verified A: INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING genuinely raises no error for the losing row (confirmed via Postgres speculative-insertion semantics and TypeORM InsertQueryBuilder.js line 330, which emits the onConflict string verbatim after ON CONFLICT with no wrapping try/catch needed). B: arbiter target ('tenant_id', ((metadata ->> 'bullmq_job_id'))) WHERE (metadata ->> 'bullmq_job_id') IS NOT NULL is structurally/semantically identical to the migration's index expression after Postgres's parse-time normalization of quoting and parenthesization (unquoted lowercase metadata == quoted "metadata"; extra parens are dropped) -- verified entity column names (NotificationEntity in entities.ts) match raw returning('*') keys used (saved.id, saved.created_at). C: walked the concurrent-insert interleaving against DatabaseContextService.runInTenantContext (database-context.service.ts) -- the losing INSERT statement blocks on the winner's row lock until the winner's transaction commits/rolls back, so the fallback SELECT in the same statement/transaction reliably sees the committed winner row under READ COMMITTED; no poisoned-transaction risk since ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING never raises 23505. D: confirmed both notifications.processor.spec.ts and dunning.service.spec.ts fully mock the query-builder chain (insert/into/values/onConflict/returning/execute) -- the raw SQL fragment's syntax/arbiter-match correctness is never exercised against real Postgres; no e2e test found. Filed as find-ae9be779 (LOW, residual gap per task instructions, not a functional defect). E: confirmed the concurrent MM changes to entities.ts (naming normalization: TransactionTipo->TransactionType, documentos->documents, status enum renames) are pre-existing unrelated changes from an earlier commit and do not touch NotificationEntity or this code path -- no interaction. Ran the three specified spec files: 3 suites / 36 tests passed. Attempted to construct a failure scenario for jobId undefined (no bullmq_job_id key -> partial index predicate false -> insert always succeeds, never enters conflict path) and for the fallback SELECT returning null (winner rolls back after all, or row deleted mid-race) -- both are extremely low-probability edge cases with no evidence of active occurrence and not worse than the prior implementation's failure modes. No reproducible functional defect found in the new atomic ON CONFLICT mechanism itself.
